brief: SEB's EM strategy desk argues US-Iran diplomacy is deadlocked inside an unstable equilibrium: Iran will not accept peace without regime stability, the US will not accept peace without regime compliance. Iran's proposal for an accelerated version of the MoU was rejected by Trump, Qatari-mediated weekend talks produced no progress, and the US ordered Iran's UN delegation out of New York, which Iran denies was coercive. Strait of Hormuz traffic has recovered to roughly two-thirds of pre-war levels and Brent holds near $100/bbl, but SEB says this is not a return to normality given elevated tanker insurance costs and continued Iranian attacks on shipping. SEB's core call: renewed US strikes are more likely to provoke large-scale Iranian retaliation against regional energy infrastructure and widen the conflict than to produce a deal, making October volatile. Iran analysts warn of a post-midterm (Nov 3) escalation once Trump is freed from electoral constraints. SEB's best case is that strikes catalyze negotiations; its more likely case is that strikes fail to coerce the regime and Iran retaliates, though damage to Iran's own energy infrastructure from that retaliation could reduce Iran's incentive to escalate first.
